summary: Reviewed frozen specification 4127ad60c80de1fea7a209919ccb83d841fa3b422f67a5a7541b37a46e5d1db8. AGENTS.md conditions restoring the marker on a new explicit project-owner decision; the owner made that decision in this session, so the task is authorised on its face rather than an agent-initiated relaxation, and the specification records the decision and its boundary rather than merely asserting permission. The scope is exactly the six files that carry the governance-mode fact: the marker itself, the three prose statements that must agree with each other (AGENTS.md, README.md, the ai-flow Skill), the entry-file contract test whose current assertion not BOOTSTRAP_MARKER.exists() would otherwise fail, and the changelog. Leaving .github/workflows/ai-quality-gate.yml out of scope is correct and important: the bootstrap branch and its quality checks already exist in the workflow, so this change activates an existing path rather than adding one, and the workflow contract tests that pin the four bootstrap_active guards stay untouched. The specification is accurate about what is and is not relaxed. I confirmed against the workflow that the bootstrap path still runs the full pytest suite with branch coverage and --cov-fail-under=85, diff-cover at 90, git diff --check, ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy; what it skips is task resolution, verify --ci and the Gate. I confirmed by grep that src/aiflow and tools contain no bootstrap awareness, so the CLI remains fully usable and this is purely a CI-layer bypass. The marker must be bare unquoted values because CI matches whole lines with grep -qx, and the existing fail-closed detection test already pins that; the specification states it and the acceptance conditions check it. The rollback is symmetric and honest: deleting the marker restores formal governance, and because detection reads the base SHA the rollback PR itself runs under the bootstrap path while the PR after it runs formal. One risk deserves naming and the specification names it: high-risk actions, branch protection and evidence-retention conventions are explicitly not relaxed, and the AI Flow CLI stays available for changes that warrant a record. Verification requirements are asserted false, giving V1; that is right because the change is covered by deterministic entry-file and workflow contract tests and touches none of the safeguards the targeted mutation manifest covers. The governance weight is carried by the REVIEW route the impact_categories [ci] rule forces, not by the verification level. The implementation must keep the marker to exactly the two canonical lines and must leave every existing bootstrap detection assertion in tests/integration/test_github_workflow.py unchanged.
